newsitem.title: USA: Load of US corporate debt supply to hit buyers mkt.
newsitem.headline: Load of US corporate debt supply to hit buyers mkt.

text.p: A load of corporate debt supply is set to hit a buyer's market this week as issuers continue to meet investor demand while rushing to get deals done before interest rates head higher, dealers said.
"I think for the first time it's more of a buyers market...they can be a little more selective," said one syndicate source. "Issuers are now more cautious about where they're pricing their deals."
About $2.0 billion in new high-yield offerings are lined up to come to market with another $1.1 billion in high-grade issues on the horizon as well, dealers said.
"There's still a positive tone out there even though the (Treasury) market has traded off a bit," said one high-grade trader. "People want to get their business done."

Among upcoming investment grade offerings, Petro Geo-Services is expected to issue $300 million in Baa3/BBB-minus rated 10-year senior unsecured notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, sources said.

Fletcher Challenge is also expected to tap the market with a $320 million Baa2/BBB rated debt offering via Merrill Lynch & Co. The deal is expected to consist of $200 million in 10-year debt and $120 million in 20-year debt, sources said.

Korea Export-Import Bank is also expected to tap the market with a $500 million A1-A-minus rated $500 million global 10-year global debt issue, puttable in the fifth year. Lehman Brothers is expected to underwrite the deal.
Turning to the high-yield sector, Gulf Canada Resoruces Ltd is expected to tap the market with a US$225 million in Ba1/BB-plus senior notes due 2017 via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Also, Central Tractor Farm & Country is expected to issue $100 million in B1/B-plus rated senior notes due 2007 via Nationsbanc Capital markets, sources said.

Intercel Inc said on Monday it planned to issue $300 million in senior notes due 2007. The company's roadshow is set to begin on March 21st and will be underwritten by lead manager Morgan Stanley & Co.
Also, Quest Communications is expected to issue a $450 million two-part 144a debt offering via Salomon Brothers.
The B2/B-plus rated deal consists $200 million in 10-year senior notes and $250 million (proceeds) of 10-year senior discount notes.
